Συναυλία

«ΖΗΤΩ ΤΑ ΛΑΪΚΑ ΚΟΡΙΤΣΙΑ» ΠΑΝΤΕΛΗΣ ΑΜΠΑΖΗΣ & ΑΝΩΤΑΤΗ ΖΑΜΠΕΤΙΚΗ

Παρασκευή 13 Φεβρουαρίου στις 00:00 | Theatre Of The No

Theatre of the No hides opposite City Hall on a street you've probably walked past without noticing. Tonight the entrance glows with arriving guests. Inside, maybe a hundred seats face a stage where Greek music tradition is about to be honored differently.

"Long Live the Laiko Girls" celebrates the women whose voices defined Greek popular music — singers whose interpretations still echo through cafes and kitchens across Greece. Pantelis Ampazis leads the Anotati Zambetiki ensemble through this tribute, bringing technical precision to material that lives on emotion. The title declares its intentions: this is homage without irony.

The crowd here crosses the usual demographic divisions. You'll find music school students who came for the technique next to grandmothers who lived through the original recordings. Theatre of the No attracts this mix — Athens' first English-speaking theater, the venue maintains accessibility while hosting work rooted in Greek tradition. By the third song, strangers are exchanging glances of recognition.

The venue's scale creates intimacy that amplifies the material's emotional weight. When a singer reaches for the notes that made these songs famous, the room is small enough to feel the effort. No distance buffers the performance — you're in it, not watching it.

If you need contemporary production or English lyrics, this concert speaks a different language. The "laiko girls" whose memory this night honors sang in Greek for Greek audiences about Greek experiences. But if you're ready to understand what those voices meant — why they still matter — Theatre of the No provides the context.
